key_insight: A split-head quantum GAN separates lattice-scale and atom-scale generation, and the quantum component mainly boosts structural diversity while the classical ablation is better at thermodynamic precision.
engineering_relevance: This architecture suggests a resource-efficient route for crystalline materials discovery on near-term hardware by combining physics-informed priors with quantum feature mapping.
method: Quantum trunk feeds a split-head generator that decouples cell bounds from atomic coordinates.
Compared SH-QGAN against an architecture-matched classical ablation to isolate the effect of quantum circuits.
Tested on the constrained Mg-Mn-O materials system to probe validity, novelty, and stoichiometric convergence.
evidence_signal: On Mg-Mn-O, the classical ablation achieved better thermodynamic precision, while SH-QGAN more than doubled geometric validity and produced novel metastable candidates near Mg2MnO4.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen architectural priors and the limited evaluation system, so gains may not directly transfer to broader crystal chemistries or larger-scale 3D generation.
paper_title: Split-Head Quantum Generative Adversarial Network for Crystalline Material Discovery
